questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Vidya put on her mask, / sanitize her hands / and walked into the shop.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** "Sanitize her hands."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of 'Sanitize' is incorrect instead of it use 'Sanitized'
 
• According to the rule of parallelism, Whenever the verbs are in parallel then we need to use all the verbs in the same form. Here, put is in the second form as we can get a hint from the verb walked as it is given in the second form also it is connected with the conjunction 'and'
 
• **Hence, the correct sentence is-** *Vidya put on her mask, **sanitized** her hands and walked into the shop.*

• The second sentence will be Sentence A as the year mentioned in this sentence is '1955'
 
• The third sentence will be sentence C as the year menioned in this sentence is '1991' also tells that in this year the parliamentary system has been established.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Ravi drove the car towards the highway for a trial run.

options.text: The car had been driven for a trial run by Ravi towards the highway.
The car had driven towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.
The car was driving towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.
The car was driven towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The car was driven towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice.
 
• While changing the sentence into passive voice the main thing you have to keep in mind is the tense of the sentence because it doesn't change.
 
• In the given sentence, the tense of the sentence is in the past tense.
 
• Hence, the structure will be- was + V₃.
 
• Also, the object of the sentence will become the subject of the sentence. The object is 'The car' and the subject is 'Ravi'

***Hence, the correct passive of the sentence is- **The car was driven towards the highway for a trial run by Ravi.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence indirect speech.**

The customer asked the bank manager if they were working on the following Saturday

options.text: The customer asked the bank manager, “Are they working on the previous Saturday?”
The customer asks the bank manager, “If you were working on the following Saturday?”
The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”
The customer said to the bank manager, “Were they working on the previous Saturday?”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is*** *'The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Indirect speech.
 
• As the given sentence has 'if' it means the interrogative reported speech will be there in Direct speech.
 
• The pronoun will be used according to the object that is 'Bank manager' so the pronoun will be 'You'
 
• The tense will be the present continuous tense.
 
• The reporting verb 'asked' will be changed into 'said to'.

**So the correct answer is-*** The customer said to the bank manager, “Are you working next Saturday?”*
